newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market at standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market at standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Friday were at a standstill, with no sales reported following active sales midweek at lower prices, feedlot sources said.
Feedlot cattle prices Wednesday fell $2.00 to $71.00 per cwt from last week's top of $73.00. Sales also were active early Thursday at $71.00.

Monday's fed cattle market was expected to stay quiet as the trade evaluates weekend beef clearance and packers look over showlists. Packers may bid $70.00 per cwt early in the week with cattle feeders likely to ask $72.00, sources said.
Cattle slaughter rebounded quickly following cutbacks on Monday that packers instituted to improve operating margins, sources said.
Packers reportedly slaughtered near capacity Wednesday through Friday to fill previously booked beef orders, they said. However, beef prices fell amid a lack of new business, the market sources said.

USDA estimated Friday's slaughter at 133,000 head, above 129,000 a week ago as well as a year ago. The figure brought the week-to-date cattle slaughter estimate to 641,000 head, up from 636,000 a week ago but lower than 675,000 a year ago.
Midday boxed beef values Friday were quoted down $0.29 to $0.56 per cwt on 50 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. Heavyweight choice cuts were quoted down $0.57 at $107.98 - a $1.92 drop for the week.
